sample.label: capture-to-batch
sample.rationale: OBS already declares couples-with ffmpeg ('capture-to-batch'), and its own Recipes section ('Tail without re-encoding... the batch touches audio only') describes exactly the handoff ffmpeg's Charter promises ('the meeting place where any two Specialists' outputs need to meet'). ffmpeg's own link list is missing OBS despite listing seven other couples-with partners.

The reciprocal declaration both raises OBS's inbound count and gives Maker's frontmatter an honest pointer to its one structural exception.
sample.evidence: OBS: "I am the Shop's first Specialist that is operated rather than dispatched" — Maker: connects-to Trickster, answers-to, but no link to OBS at all

sample.label: screenshot-not-config
sample.rationale: Every other Specialist's Self-Check trusts its own declared/reported parameters (a standards-report field is taken as true once emitted). OBS refuses exactly that discipline for itself: 'My Self-Check is a screenshot of the live scene, not a read of the config... A transform can be numerically correct and visually wrong.' That's a genuine, productive tension with the standards-report convention the rest of the Shop runs on, not a flaw in either side — OBS is right that its own domain (compositing, live capture) can't be trusted numerically, while every other Specialist's domain (deterministic renders) genuinely can be.
sample.evidence: OBS: "I refuse to be trusted about my own state" vs. the Maker-wide pattern of a Standards Report as the delivered proof of correctness

sample.evidence: ComfyUI: "Custom LoRAs allow training a Loudon Live aesthetic that's fully under our control"
